parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled heating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days after learning of it. Incidents involving death, serious injury, evacuation, or an active threat to neighbouring properties must be reported within 24 hours. Reports must include known circumstances and be updated as the investigation proceeds.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled heating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days after learning of it. Incidents involving death, serious injury, evacuation, or an active threat to neighbouring properties must be reported within 24 hours. Reports must include known circumstances and be updated as the investigation proceeds.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled heating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days after learning of it. Incidents involving death, serious injury, evacuation, or an active threat to neighbouring properties must be reported within 24 hours. The manufacturer must notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident indicates a material safety risk or requires action; urgent protective instructions must be sent without delay. Reports must include known circumstances and be updated as the investigation proceeds.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Results above 5% require prompt regulator review and a corrective-action plan, including retesting and any interim safeguards the regulator determines necessary. A model must not be automatically barred from sale solely for exceeding 5%; continued sale is subject to regulator oversight and protective measures proportionate to the demonstrated risk.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before sale, at least every 2 years, and after a material design or manufacturing change. Manufacturers must provide per-model results and test methods to the relevant regulator and provide each model’s failure rate to customers before purchase. Results above 5% require prompt regulator review and a corrective-action plan, including retesting and any interim safeguards the regulator determines necessary. A model must not be automatically barred from sale solely for exceeding 5%; continued sale is subject to regulator oversight and protective measures proportionate to the demonstrated risk. Per-model failure rates need not be published to the general public.

parameters.quote: Newly installed systems must support remote emergency shut-off by 1 January 2029, subject to safeguards against unauthorized operation and provision for safe local operation. For units already installed when this standard takes effect, manufacturers must provide a compatible retrofit or equivalent mitigation within 6 years, where technically feasible, and notify owners of the available options and any limitations.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: Newly installed systems must support remote emergency shut-off by 1 January 2029, subject to safeguards against unauthorized operation and provision for safe local operation. For units already installed when this standard takes effect, manufacturers must provide a compatible retrofit or equivalent mitigation within 6 years, where technically feasible, and notify owners of the available options and any limitations.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: Newly installed systems must support remote emergency shut-off by 1 January 2029, subject to safeguards against unauthorized operation and provision for safe local operation. For units already installed when this standard takes effect, manufacturers must provide a compatible retrofit or equivalent mitigation within 6 years, where technically feasible, and notify owners of the available options and any limitations.

parameters.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard is adopted.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard is adopted.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard is adopted. The suppression system must be suitable for the battery chemistry and designed not to create additional hazards. Manufacturers must provide evidence of its effectiveness and maintenance requirements to the relevant regulator and disclose those requirements to customers.

parameters.quote: A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Manufacturers must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, explain the remedy and timeline, and report progress until the recall is complete.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Manufacturers must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, explain the remedy and timeline, and report progress until the recall is complete.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase, customers must receive clear safety information for the specific model, including its per-model thermal test failure rate, material risks, required maintenance, emergency instructions, and how to report an incident. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks and provide protective instructions without delay. A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Manufacturers must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, explain the remedy and timeline, and report progress until the recall is complete. A recall requires prompt protective action and corrective measures; following regulator review and verification that the risk is adequately addressed, the model may return to sale.

ground_truth_claims.message_text: For evidence-based discussion, Halcyon’s flagship has a 3.9% failure rate in the 55°C sustained-heat test and recorded 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year. A mandatory recall trigger should be treated as a customer-protection remedy, not an automatic market ban; the standard should specify proportionate remedies and a path to return after corrective action. judge_section_notes: The final S2 removes any automatic sales ban for models above 5% (the threshold now only triggers regulator review and corrective action), which protects Northwind's 6.2% Hearth 10 and is the main gain for Northwind. S3 gives installed units a 6-year retrofit window, and S5 imposes a mandatory recall at 8 per 100k with no transition, which would capture Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9. The new-unit shut-off date is given as a calendar date (1 January 2029) with no adoption date, so its months-from-adoption value is left null.
